item.title: Will Saints owner Gayle Benson’s surprise message to Kellen Moore after harsh criticism be kiss of death?
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Will Saints owner Gayle Benson’s surprise message to Kellen Moore after harsh criticism be kiss of death? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson has publicly backed head coach Kellen Moore despite recently criticizing the team’s disappointing start. Her apparent vote of confidence comes days after Benson warned the Saints that their performances were unacceptable. The Saints entered Week 6 with a 1-4 record, including three consecutive losses. Benson’s earlier remarks raised questions about Moore’s job security and the franchise’s direction. However, Benson appeared at Friday’s practice to embrace Moore and express her support for the coaching staff , according to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The public endorsement reportedly indicated that no immediate coaching change was expected. Her gesture contrasted with Tuesday’s criticism, when she emphasized accountability throughout the organization. “We are 1-4, and that is not acceptable to me, and falls short of what our fans truly deserve,” Benson said. Despite her support, Benson maintained that improved performances remain essential. “Words will not restore our fans’ confidence. Our performance must do that,” she added. The Saints have struggled defensively, allowing 30.2 points per game, the NFL’s second-highest average entering Sunday. Offensively, quarterback Tyler Shough and his teammates committed eight turnovers during their three-game losing streak. Injuries have compounded those problems, with Travis Etienne and Kelvin Banks Jr. on injured reserve. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson has also missed time with a hamstring injury. The Saints previously faced questions about their offensive struggles following their disappointing start. Although Benson’s endorsement offers reassurance, it does not guarantee Moore’s long-term future. New Orleans finished 6-11 in Moore’s first season but won five of its final eight games, raising expectations for 2026. For now, Moore retains ownership’s support. However, continued losses could renew scrutiny of his position. The Saints face the New York Giants on Sunday, providing another opportunity to respond on the field. item.title: Giants RB update is bad news for Cam Skattebo for Week 6 vs. Saints
item.description: Giants RB update is bad news for Cam Skattebo for Week 6 vs. Saints originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Heading into Week 6, the New York Giants sit in first place in the NFC East and are looking to build on their lead with a very winnable game against the New Orleans Saints . While Jaxson Dart is still out, Jameis Winston and this offense have been perfectly suitable for the season so far. But looking at the running back rotation, it appears that some change is on the way, and it's not good for Cam Skattebo. According to ESPN's Jordan Raanan , the Giants are making a change at running back, with Skattebo set to get less work than normal after his fumbling issues nearly cost the Giants the game in Week 5 against the Washington Commanders . Giants to shake up RB room after Cam Skattebo's fumbling issues "Expectation is there will be a change to the Giants' RB rotation, per sources," Raanan reports. "Najee Harris is likely to have a larger role, with Cam Skattebo downgraded but still part of the mix after the fumbles." This is some unexpected news for the Giants, but it isn't a complete surprise. Skattebo has four fumbles this season through five games, and his fumble in overtime of Week 5 against the Commanders might've been the last straw. With the Giants well within field goal range with a chance to win the game, Skattebo fumbled the ball. The Commanders then marched down the field, and if it weren't for an all-time horrible mistake, the Giants would've lost. MORE : Mike Evans trolls Trevon Diggs with classic 'Who are you?' jersey check in viral exchange John Harbaugh has seen enough and is making a change that's bad news for Skattebo. The fan-favorite running back will still be involved in the offense, but he's no longer going to be the lead back. Najee Harris is set to take over the main share of this backfield, though he'll be splitting time with Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, and Devin Singletary, as all four running backs are set to be active Sunday for the Giants. While the Giants shaking the RB room up is a bit of a surprise, considering Skattebo's fumbling issues so far this season, it makes sense why the Giants are going away from him, at least for now, until he can be trusted again. item.title: ‘Arch Manning is a bad football player’: Criticism mounts for Arch Manning after another loss
item.description: Syndication: Austin American-Statesman Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning entered the season as the favorite to go No. 1 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft. But after back-to-back losses in which his turnovers proved costly, the criticism of the Texas star has reached a new level. Following Saturday’s 27-24 home loss to the Florida Gators, analysts and former players across the sport lined up to take shots at Manning, with some questioning whether he’s even an NFL prospect and one calling him “a bad football player.” Arch Manning’s Struggles Texas jumped out to a 17-3 lead over Florida on Saturday, but the Gators, led by backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. in his first career start, rattled off 24 straight points. Manning had a chance to answer on the final drive, but he fumbled, and Florida recovered to seal the upset. Manning finished 14-for-20 for 173 yards and a touchdown. The loss came just one week after his late interception helped Oklahoma beat Texas, and he has topped 250 passing yards in just one of his last five games. After the game, head coach Steve Sarkisian didn’t rule out benching Manning , saying that “everything is going to be evaluated.” ‘Can we start being real?’ Adam Kramer of Bleacher Report had a rather scathing review of Manning’s performance, as he argued that Manning’s time at Texas “should be nearing an end.” However, he certainly wasn’t the only one criticizing the “I say this with seriousness. If Arch Manning gets drafted anywhere in the first 5 rounds the NFL is a nepo baby system. Arch Manning is a bad football player can we start being real?” wrote Breiden Fehoko , a former LSU defensive tackle and NFL veteran. “Texas and Arch way too many missed reads. Way too many open, simple completions passed up trying to play hero ball. Way too many times his eyes are in the wrong place. While he has spectacular plays every week, his inability to sustain the routine plays and reads is extremely concerning,” wrote former NFL quarterback Sean Salisbury of QB Confessions. “Arch Manning needs to stay at Texas for a 3rd year. He’s not NFL ready,” wrote Jon Root of OutKick. “Arch Manning and Bryce Underwood, meeting up in the portal this winter,” wrote Aaron Torres of Fox Sports Radio. “Tried to tell yall about Arch Manning three years ago,” wrote Barrett Sallee of CBS Sports. Clearly, the Manning name isn’t buying Arch much patience anymore. item.title: Arsenal and Chelsea both keen on 17-year-old midfielder
item.description: Arsenal and Chelsea both keen on 17-year-old midfielder Arsenal and Chelsea Tracking Oliver Mansson as Swedish Midfield Talent Draws Premier League Interest Arsenal and Chelsea have developed a serious interest in Oliver Mansson, the teenage IFK Göteborg midfielder who is beginning to stir the kind of attention that can alter a young career in a heartbeat. According to TEAMtalk , both London clubs have been impressed by the 17-year-old Swede, a player whose early rise has already alerted several Premier League scouts. There is something familiar about this sort of story. A composed young midfielder emerges in Scandinavia, settles quickly into senior football and suddenly the biggest clubs in England start circling. Yet what makes Mansson especially intriguing is how quickly he appears to have adapted to the demands of first-team football. He made his senior debut at 16 earlier this summer and has continued to build momentum under Joachim Björklund at IFK Göteborg. Oliver Mansson emerging as a serious Arsenal target Mansson plays as a holding midfielder and already seems to carry many of the attributes elite clubs crave. At 6ft, he has the frame to cope physically as he matures, but it is the refinement in his game that has brought him into sharper focus. His touch, awareness and ability to manage possession from deep have all been noted, and there is a growing sense that he can influence matches with calm authority beyond his age. Photo: IMAGO For Arsenal, that sort of profile will naturally appeal. Mikel Arteta has consistently valued midfielders who can receive under pressure, move the ball cleanly and read the rhythm of a game before it begins to run away. Chelsea, too, remain alert to high-upside youth opportunities, particularly when a player combines technical security with room for major development. Premier League scouts increasing focus on Swedish midfielder Arsenal and Chelsea are far from alone. Tottenham Hotspur, Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland have also monitored Mansson in recent weeks, a sign that his emergence is being taken seriously across England. When interest stretches that widely, it usually speaks to more than one impressive performance. It suggests a player is building a body of work that demands attention. That wider Premier League interest matters because it creates a different kind of pressure around a young footballer. item.title: Allegri did not lead Napoli training after Venezia loss and faces increasing risk of sack
item.description: Allegri did not lead Napoli training after Venezia loss and faces increasing risk of sack The latest reports confirm that Massimiliano Allegri did not lead Napoli’s recovery session on Sunday morning after Saturday’s defeat against Venezia due to illness, whilst newspapers in Italy suggest that coach has two difficult games to turn his Partenopei career around. Allegri skips Napoli training with illness but faces increasing pressure Napoli were beaten 1-0 in Serie A on Saturday by a Venezia side that had not picked up a single point in any of their first six league games of the season. VENICE, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli misses the penalty during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on October 17, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Before the Venezia match, Allegri had already matched the worst start to a Napoli season in 17 years by suffering four defeats in his first eight games in charge across all competitions. That figure has now risen to five defeats from nine matches. With a record of three wins, one draw and three defeats in Serie A so far this season, Napoli are already nine points shy of Inter at the top of the Serie A standings. They have also lost twice in the Champions League, which means they can barely afford to drop any more points until the end of the league phase if they are to qualify for the round of 16. The upcoming schedule is also a cause for concern. Napoli are in Champions League action against Bodo Glimt on Tuesday. This is already considered a must-win game against a side that beat reigning Serie A champions home and away in the Champions League play-off round last season. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, reacts during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 10, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) After that is a difficult Serie A test against an in-form Roma side at the Stadio Maradona on Saturday (October 24). La Gazzetta dello Sport writes that a turnaround in results is now ‘urgent’ and that Allegri’s future as head coach of Napoli ‘will be at risk’ without a positive result from the next two matches. To make life even more complicated, Allegri was unable to lead Napoli’s training session on Sunday after the 1-0 defeat against Venezia on Saturday as he is currently suffering with the flu according to reports from the Corriere dello Sport.

item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Karlsruher SC cruise past Darmstadt to end losing streak
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Karlsruher SC cruise past Darmstadt to end losing streak Shio Fukuda and Marvin Wanitzek gave the hosts a commanding advantage inside the opening 13 minutes, before Christoph Kobald and Kevin Wiethaup added further goals after the interval. The result ends Karlsruhe’s three-game losing streak in the league and provides a significant boost for Maximilian Senft’s side. Karlsruhe made the perfect start to the contest and took the lead in the sixth minute. Marvin Wanitzek helped create the opportunity with a neat lay-off on the edge of the penalty area, allowing Fukuda to take aim from a half-left position and fire a low finish into the near corner beyond Marcel Schuhen. The hosts continued to apply pressure and doubled their advantage just seven minutes later. Noel Eichinger’s effort initially caused problems for the Darmstadt goalkeeper, who was unable to hold the ball. Fukuda subsequently helped work the opportunity into Wanitzek’s path, with the Karlsruhe captain firing into the far corner to make it 2-0. Darmstadt attempted to respond, but Karlsruhe remained organised and continued to look dangerous going forward. The visitors struggled to find a way through the hosts’ defence, leaving Florian Kohfeldt’s side with a significant task as they headed into the break two goals behind. Karlsruhe carried their momentum into the second half and effectively put the contest beyond doubt five minutes after the restart. Kobald found the net in the 50th minute to extend the hosts’ advantage to three goals, leaving Darmstadt facing an uphill battle. The home side showed little sign of easing off and added a fourth in the 65th minute through Wiethaup. With a four-goal cushion already established, Karlsruhe were able to manage the remainder of the contest without allowing Darmstadt a route back into the game. The visitors searched for a consolation goal during the closing stages, but Karlsruhe held firm to preserve their clean sheet and complete an impressive afternoon at the BBBank Wildpark. The result represents a major response from Senft’s side after consecutive setbacks, with the emphatic victory lifting Karlsruhe off the bottom of the table and offering renewed confidence ahead of their next fixture. For Darmstadt, the defeat is a disappointing setback following their 3-1 victory over Energie Cottbus last weekend. Kohfeldt’s side were unable to reproduce that performance in Baden, with their defensive struggles in the opening stages ultimately proving costly.

item.title: What Rutgers football QB Dylan Lonergan showed in win over Maryland
item.description: COLLEGE PARK, Maryland – There was no panic, and there was no spiral. Instead Dylan Lonergan bounced back. The Rutgers football quarterback threw a second quarter interception that Maryland capitalized on with a touchdown, but Lonergan recovered well and played his best game of the season in the Scarlet Knights’ 37-30 win over the Terrapins on Saturday at SECU Stadium. “I felt very comfortable today,” Lonergan said. “I felt like I bounced back well from the interception. But other than that, I felt really good.” It showed. And that’s good news for the Scarlet Knights ’ offense. This hasn’t been an easy season for Lonergan, as the Boston College transfer threw five interceptions in his first two games. But Lonergan has steadily improved in Kirk Ciarrocca’s offense, and instead of letting another interception ruin his afternoon, Lonergan settled in and calmly went to work against Maryland’s defense. Lonergan finished 23-of-35 for 291 yards and three touchdowns. Did he feel this was his best game of the season? “If you discount (FCS-level) Howard, for sure,” Lonergan said. “Excited to keep building on this.” One of Lonergan’s biggest passes came in the third quarter. Rutgers had third-and-10 at its own 33. Lonergan rolled to the left and delivered a dart to KJ Duff for a 26-yard pass that gave the Scarlet Knights a first down at the Terrapins 41. “Those are the kinds of plays experienced quarterbacks make,” coach Greg Schiano said. “I was pleased to see that.” Three plays later Lonergan hit running back Clay Thevenin in the end zone for a 19-yard touchdown pass that tied the game at 23. Thevenin was one of seven players who caught passes from Lonergan. Duff led that group with nine catches for 113 yards and two touchdowns. “Every time I was throwing the ball, I was throwing to someone different,” Lonergan said. “It was awesome being able to spread the ball around. I feel confident in everybody to make plays.” That confidence should pay dividends as the season progresses. Nothing is getting easier for the Scarlet Knights anytime soon. The travel to play Northwestern in their next game before hosting Michigan at home, then facing Wisconsin on the road. But Rutgers needed better quarterback play, and Lonergan is showing that improvement. He said after the Maryland win that it took some time learning the Rutgers offense – that process even lasted throughout fall camp. “I think every day I’m still learning, still building on it,” Lonergan said. The more comfortable he feels and the more confident he is in his receivers, the better the Scarlet Knights’ offense will be. How much this performance serves as a springboard the rest of the season remains to be seen. At the very least it was a step in the right direction. “He’s getting more comfortable,” Schiano said. “We just have to keep doing it. Not just him, but the entire team. We just have to keep doing it.” This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: What Rutgers football QB Dylan Lonergan sho

item.title: Big 12 confirms Notre Dame got totally screwed by clock gaffe at end of BYU loss
item.description: MICHAEL CLUBB/SOUTH BEND TRIBUNE / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Big 12 confirms Notre Dame got totally screwed by clock gaffe at end of BYU loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The No. 3 Notre Dame Fighting Irish suffered a 28-24 defeat to No. 8 BYU in a game that was marred with controversy. Aside from a questionable no-call pass interference on the final play of the game, the Fighting Irish were also on the wrong end of a clock gaffe that denied them one more play. In the aftermath of the game, the Big 12 acknowledged that the referees made a big mistake by not putting one second back on the game clock after that play. “Following the Big 12’s review of the final play of Saturday’s Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew,” the statement read, per The Athletic. “The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week’s games.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Replays of the final play showed the ball intended for Irish wide receiver Jaden Greathouse hit the turf with one second left on the clock. Based on the rule, Notre Dame should’ve had one more play on the BYU 8-yard line. After going down 21-10 at halftime, the Fighting Irish staged a second-half comeback and took a 24-21 lead early in the fourth quarter. However, the Cougars answered with a Walker Lyons touchdown with under two minutes remaining to deal Notre Dame its first loss of the season. Coach Marcus Freeman and the Fighting Irish will have the week off to regroup before facing off against Navy on Halloween. item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Dynamo Dresden end winless run with derby victory over Magdeburg
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Dynamo Dresden end winless run with derby victory over Magdeburg Niklas Hauptmann opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the ninth minute, before Simon Straudi doubled Dynamo’s advantage shortly after the interval. Thomas Stamm’s side then held firm to claim all three points in front of 30,651 supporters at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion, recording their first clean sheet since the second matchday. The hosts made an ideal start to the contest and were awarded a penalty in the ninth minute following a VAR review. Magdeburg defender Tobias Müller caught Nicolai Rapp on the leg while attempting to clear the ball, prompting the referee to consult the pitchside monitor before pointing to the spot. Hauptmann stepped up and confidently converted the penalty to give Dresden an early advantage, continuing his recent scoring form after also finding the net against Osnabrück last weekend. Magdeburg responded by taking greater control of possession and attempting to work their way back into the contest. However, despite enjoying spells on the ball, the visitors struggled to turn their dominance into clear-cut opportunities against a disciplined Dresden defence. The hosts remained dangerous on the counterattack and gradually regained their initiative towards the end of the first half, heading into the break with their slender advantage intact. Dresden carried that momentum into the second period and doubled their lead just five minutes after the restart. A cross from Jonas Sterner was not properly dealt with by the Magdeburg defence, allowing Straudi to collect the loose ball on the edge of the penalty area before firing a low effort beyond goalkeeper Dominik Reimann in the 50th minute. The goal left Magdeburg with a significant challenge as they searched for a route back into the game, but Dresden continued to threaten on the break. Vincent Vermeij had an excellent opportunity to put the contest beyond doubt in the 68th minute after being released by a long pass from Sterner. The forward brought the ball under control and raced through on goal, but his effort was struck straight at Reimann, allowing the Magdeburg goalkeeper to keep his side in the match. Nevertheless, Dresden remained defensively organised throughout the closing stages and prevented the visitors from finding a breakthrough, seeing out the contest to secure a valuable derby victory. The result ends Dynamo’s five-match winless streak and provides a significant boost for Stamm’s side, who move out of the relegation places with their first clean sheet since the second matchday. For Magdeburg, the defeat is a setback after their 3-0 victory over Hannover 96 last weekend. Despite enjoying considerable possession, they were unable to make their territorial advantage count as Dresden proved more clinical in the decisive moments.

item.title: Sonay Kartal’s dream run to Wuhan Open final ends in defeat to Maja Chwalinska
item.description: Sonay Kartal ’s brilliant run at the Wuhan Open ended in a bruising three-set loss to French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska. The Briton dominated the first set but was reeled back in thanks to a gritty performance from 16th seed Chwalinska, who converted her third match point at the end of a nervy final game to win 2-6 6-4 6-2. The 25-year-old, who beat world No 11 Iva Jovic and six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek to make her first WTA 1000 final, collapsed to the court in relief as she sealed the title in two hours and 43 minutes. While a disappointing result for Kartal this week has nonetheless been a superb step up in only her third tournament since a six-month injury layoff following a stress fracture in her back. She had never previously gone beyond the quarter-finals at a WTA 1000 event, the level below the majors. The 24-year-old did it the hard way, dispatching three seeded players in a row in former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic , two-time major finalist Jasmine Paolini and world No 6 Elina Svitolina , before beating former French Open winner Jelena Ostapenko in the semi-finals. Having been ranked 170th in the world after her injury lay-off Kartal was the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 finalist since the format was introduced 17 years ago, and only the second British woman ever to make a final at this level after Johanna Konta. She will climb to 50th in the world when the rankings are updated on Monday and replace Katie Boulter as the British No 1. Momentum swung repeatedly over the course of the encounter, with nine breaks in the first 18 games. Kartal was superior in the first set against a flat Chwalinska but the Pole came out fighting in the second, with her unusual, crafty style, changes of pace and direction and lefty serve causing problems. Kartal was broken in a mammoth game at 3-3 but upped her aggression to break straight back, only to be on the receiving end of a third straight break thanks to an unlucky net cord at 40-15. Chwalinska deployed the drop shot to great effect and forced a deciding set with a tidy backhand volley at the net. Chwalinska fell to the ground in relief as she converted her third championship point (Reuters) After a run of four straight holds Kartal was first to blink in the decider, with the Briton broken to love as she shanked a forehand wide for 2-3. Chwalinska continued to impose herself, replying to a Kartal drop shot with a better one of her own to earn a break point at 4-2, and converting it immediately as she pushed Kartal behind the baseline, with the world No 170 firing long under pressure. Both players were wracked with nerves as Chwalinska served for the title: Kartal missed three break points while Chwalinska spurned her first two championship points before finally converting the third as the Brit hit long.

Last week, on the Bills postgame radio show I host, six of the eight callers had negative takes on the air. After THAT victory over the Rams. The object of these games is to win them. item.title: Britain's Kartal misses out on biggest title of her career
item.description: Sonay Kartal will become the British number one when the WTA rankings are released on Monday [Getty Images] Britain's Sonay Kartal missed out on what would have been the biggest title of her career as she faded in a gripping Wuhan Open final against French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska. Kartal, 24, was bidding to lift the trophy in only her third event since returning from a six-month absence caused by a back injury. But an extraordinary week seemed to catch up with Kartal as she ran out of steam - physically and mentally - in a 2-6 6-4 6-2 defeat. Kartal was playing in just the 10th match of her impressive comeback and was attempting to become the first Briton to win a WTA 1,000 title since Johanna Konta in 2017. Ranked 170th in the world at the start of the event, Kartal reached Sunday's final by seeing off a host of notable opponents, including current top-10 players and former major champions. However, Poland's Chwalinska, who made a shock run to this year's Roland Garros final, dragged Kartal into a brutal battle and ultimately got the better of it. Kartal dominated the first set and led by a break in the second before Chwalinska turned momentum in her favour. Chwalinska, 25, felt a few nerves as she closed in on her first WTA 1,000 title, but took her third championship point when Kartal hammered a forehand long. Despite losing the final, Kartal has enjoyed a transformational week which even she did not see coming. On Monday, Kartal will climb to 50th in the world rankings - just below her career high - and become the British number one for the first time. item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Arminia Bielefeld leave it late to edge past VfL Osnabrück Robin Meißner had given the visitors an early lead after capitalising on a defensive error, but Maximilian Bauer quickly restored parity for Oliver Kirch’s side. With the contest finely balanced heading into the closing stages, Jannik Rochelt struck late to secure all three points for the hosts. Bielefeld started on the front foot but were almost punished inside the opening stages when Stefano Russo’s under-hit back-pass presented Meißner with a golden opportunity. The Osnabrück forward intercepted the ball but could only steer his effort wide of the right-hand post. The visitors made no mistake with their next opportunity in the 16th minute. Another misplaced pass in the Bielefeld defence allowed Meißner to race through on goal, round goalkeeper Jonas Kersken and slot into the unguarded net to put Osnabrück ahead. However, the hosts responded positively and restored parity just 10 minutes later. Arne Sicker delivered a dangerous free-kick into the penalty area, where Bauer rose to meet the cross and headed home from close range to make it 1-1. The equaliser sparked a more evenly contested period, with neither side able to establish a clear advantage before the interval. Osnabrück had threatened through their pressing and ability to exploit defensive mistakes, while Bielefeld looked increasingly dangerous from set-pieces. The second half continued in a similar fashion, with both teams searching for a breakthrough. Bielefeld gradually increased the pressure and came close to taking the lead when Joel Grodowski met a teasing cross with a header, only to see his effort strike the post in the 64th minute. As the match entered its final stages, the hosts continued to push forward in search of a winner. Their persistence was eventually rewarded in the 85th minute when Rochelt found the net to put Bielefeld 2-1 ahead and send the home supporters into celebration. Osnabrück were left with little time to respond, and Bielefeld held on to secure a valuable victory in the regional rivalry. The result gives Kirch’s side consecutive league wins following their 1-0 victory away to VfL Bochum last weekend, providing further momentum after an inconsistent start to the campaign. For Osnabrück, the defeat represents a frustrating outcome after taking an early lead, with defensive mistakes ultimately proving costly as Bielefeld claimed all three points.

item.title: Barcelona coach identifies Real Madrid target as a priority ahead of January transfer window
item.description: Barcelona coach identifies Real Madrid target as a priority ahead of January transfer window Barcelona may have enjoyed a prolific start to the new season, winning 11 out of 11 matches in all competitions. But the club’s problems are mounting, with Hansi Flick notably devoid of any real depth in central defence following Andreas Christensen’s injury. Gerard Martin’s performances have fallen compared to last season while both him, Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde picked up knocks against Real Betis. Hansi Flick wants Finn Jeltsch Jeltsch is a rising star in the Bundesliga. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) The lack of depth in defence could force Barcelona to look into the transfer market once again, with Hansi Flick already picking the club’s ideal target. According to Diario SPORT , Flick has identified Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch as his preferred target in the upcoming January transfer window. It is no secret that the German tactician is a keen observer of the Bundesliga and Jeltsch, to that end, has been one of rising stars in German football, even earning a call up to the national team recently. It remains to be seen whether or not Barcelona make a move for Jeltsch in the upcoming January transfer window, but signing the defender could be a costly affair, as he is valued at around €50 million. Not to mention, Barcelona could face stiff competition from Liverpool and arch-rival Real Madrid, who have been monitoring the young defender for quite some time. Why Barcelona must remain cautious Jeltsch doesn’t have much experience at the highest level. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Despite the cost involved, Jeltsch does bring a lot of quality to the table. Standing at 1.85m, the German is an imposing figure in defence and is very useful when it comes to playing the ball out from the back. The drawback, though, is that Jeltsch is a right-sided centre-back. Barcelona, right now, are in dire need of a left-footed centre-back, who can operate alongside Pau Cubarsi. Not to mention, Jeltsch is also quite young whereas Barcelona ideally need some experience to replace Inigo Martinez. That is why the Catalans must hold off on their pursuit of the Stuttgart star and instead go after a more proven alternative. Jeltsch’s national teammate Nico Schlotterbeck, to that end, could be an ideal alternative as the Dortmund star could be available on a cut price deal next summer and is a left-footed defender, who possesses brilliant leadership qualities.

A to Z: Duncan Ferguson - 'The original Everton hero' Ferguson link has caused a 'real buzz' - McCann The appeal of bringing Ferguson's star power to the Irish Premiership is obvious, akin to the boost provided to the League of Ireland by former Chelsea winger Damian Duff's successful, if short, stint with Shelbourne in recent years. Fans quickly had their own fun with the imminent appointment on Saturday, with erroneous reports of the seven-times capped Scottish striker being spotted everywhere from his prospective new side's 1-0 win over Limavady to a local chip shop on the Newtownards Road. Glentoran are no strangers to big names in the playing ranks having had the likes of Keith Gillespie, Nacho Novo and Niall McGinn plying their trade at the Oval in recent times, but it is different when such a presence is in the dugout. Ferguson, after all, will have been the only applicant with spells as an assistant to the likes of Carlo Ancelotti, Rafa Benitez and Ronald Koeman on his CV. In all, the Scot worked under seven different permanent bosses at Everton, as well as two separate stints in interim charge. After leaving Merseyside following the departure of Frank Lampard in 2022, managerial roles at Forest Green Rovers and Inverness Caledonian Thistle were hardly considered a success, admittedly both in testing circumstances. Coupled with his unfamiliarity with the Irish League and, for all the headlines already generated, there is no doubt that the left-field appointment is a gamble. Ferguson won the FA Cup with Everton in 1995 [Getty Images] The Glentoran hierarchy clearly believe it is a risk worth taking. Some Oval regulars may well suggest that the club have tried just about everything else in their quest for a first league title since 2009. Owner Ali Shams Pour arrived a decade after the late Alan McDonald delivered the most recent of the side's 23 Gibson Cups. Since then, the turbulent reign of Mick McDermott brought Irish Cup success in 2020 yet he still was the victim of supporter protests. The calming presence of Rodney McAree delivered immediate results, but the now Dungannon boss lasted just under five months before departing for personal reasons to be replaced by Warren Feeney. Unpopular from the off owing to his previous association with bitter rivals Linfield, the 46-times capped Northern Ireland international was unable to win over the fanbase during another short reign. That brought about Devine's appointment with the County Antrim Shield triumph of January 2025 a high the club could not build upon. Consecutive losses in BetMcLean Cup finals created a sense of stalled momentum. It already feels likely to be forgotten just how close Devine came to delivering that long-sought title. A win in the penultimate league game of last season against Larne and the Glens would have gone into the final day top of the table. Instead, the disappointment of a 0-0 draw from a game in which they were the better side lingered into the subsequent performance against Coleraine and they were beaten 6-2 at the Showgrounds to ultimately finish third. It will not have escaped Ferguson's attention that one half of the league's so-called 'Big Two' have still not finished in the league's top two for 17 years. In replacing Devine, Ferguson will inherit a squad built by and for the former Derry City and Bohemians boss. And just as Devine's appointment brought about a sweeping clear-out in the summer of 2024, it is again a playing group that for all the expenditure over the past five transfer windows again feels imbalanced. An over-reliance on Jordan Stewart for a creative spark led to the September return of Conor McMenamin just two months after he had signed for Coleraine - that transfer now somehow the second most surprising story of Glentoran's season. That in turn, however, saw Joe Thomson move the other way, robbing the side of midfield drive only months after one of last season's star performers, Cammy Palmer, returned home to Scotland. Similarly, the absence of 2025-26 top scorer Pat Hoban during the early months of this season highlighted the lack of like-for-like cover given the talented Jordan Jenkins plays in an entirely different way. Four wins and a draw from their past five league games under interim boss Paddy McCourt, however, offers the reminder that most in the Irish Premiership would still happily swap their squads for the one Ferguson will now hope to rebuild into title challengers once again. Those managers will not, however, be dealing with the same expectations. Nor the same attention.

It will be interesting to see if he stays hot. Cloud #1 My first cloud goes to three, no, four straight runs up the middle when you have an opportunity to win the game. I understand you are trying to get Northwestern to burn its timeouts. How did that work out for ya? You know who else knows you’re trying to do that? Your opponent. item.description: San Diego, California - October 05: San Diego Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller looks on during a workout ahead of Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) MLB free agency cannot begin until the season concludes after the World Series, but the San Diego Padres are not waiting for the end of this season before they start building for the future. It was reported on Saturday that San Diego had agreed to a minor league deal with Japanese pitcher Tatsuya Nogami. Lincoln Zdunich of Gaslamp Ball said the numbers on Nogami are limited, but he is an intriguing prospect with a multi-pitch arsenal. When the Friar Faithful get to see Nogami in action is unknown, but Zdunich thinks there could be a chance he gets an invite to Spring Training to see what he can do against top-level MLB talent. Young controllable pitching is something the Padres have lacked in recent years due to a multitude of mid-season trades. Nogami provides that if he can be developed in the San Diego system under pitching coach Ruben Niebla. This may not be a big-name, flashy signing but it is a start. Another player who could see an opportunity to show what he can do is Alex McCoy, who has shown the ability to crush the baseball at the minor league level. Cheri Bell of Gaslamp Ball says the problem is he is still very much a swing-and-miss candidate. McCoy has been getting some headlines in the Arizona Fall League and could be someone to watch in the minor league system as the Padres push him to show more at each of the next levels. item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than Saturday’s win over Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
